title: valaki, mindenki, senki: someone, everyone, no one

sections.title: Three series built on question words
sections.content: Hungarian builds "someone", "everyone" and "no one" from question words and a prefix. *vala-* means some, *minden-* means every, and *se-* means no. You know *valahol*, *sehol*, *minden*, *mindig* and *soha* already; this screen puts them in their families.

sections.title: The se- words need nem
sections.content: A se- word goes together with *nem* before the verb, just like *soha nem*: *Senki nem válaszol*, *Sehova nem megyünk*. Without *nem* the sentence is wrong. In English one negative is enough ("nobody answers"), and Hungarian says it twice, as in *senki nem*. You will also hear *sem* instead of *nem*: *Senki sem válaszol*. The words take case endings like any noun: *valakit* ("someone", object), *valamit*, *mindenkit*, *semmit*, *valakivel*, *senkivel*.
*mindenki* takes a singular verb: *Mindenki itt van*. And *soha* is the odd one in the se- series, because it is not spelled *se-*: it is the old word you know from *soha nem*.
